 JUDGMENT This appeal is filed by the owner of the luggage carrier auto rickshaw, questioning the liability fixed on him.
2. Brief facts:
On 09.06.2009, deceased Hanumanthappa was transporting the goods belonging to his brother-Ramu from Ripponpete towards Nagavalli in a Bajaj Auto bearing Registration No.KA-15/5607 on Kargal-Bhatkal - PWD tar Road.

sentences.text: At that time, the driver of the said luggage auto drove the said vehicle in a rash and negligent manner near Channakalluhole and the said auto rickshaw was capsized and fallen to the ditch.
Hanumanthappa sustained injuries on his left fore head, right head, nose and other parts of the body.

Immediately, he was shifted to the VENLOCK Hospital,
Bangalore, but unfortunately, he succumbed to the injuries on 11.06.2009 in the hospital.
Therefore, the claimants of the deceased have filed claim petition seeking compensation.

3. Learned counsel for the appellant-owner submitted that the deceased was traveling in the luggage goods carrier auto rickshaw as an authorized representatives of the goods from Ripponpet to Nagavalli and in the meanwhile, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of auto rickshaw, the accident was caused and in the said accident, the deceased succumbed to the grievous injuries.
When the deceased was traveling in the auto rickshaw as an authorized representative of goods,
then, his risk covered under Section 147 of the M.V. Act.
Therefore, the Insurance Company is liable to pay compensation in view of existence of insurance policy.
But, the Tribunal has committed an error in fixing the liability on the appellant-owner of the auto rickshaw.
Therefore prays for modification of the liability fixed by the Tribunal.
4. It is further submitted that even though the facts are construed that the goods auto rickshaw was empty moving from Ripponpet to Nagavalli.
But, the goods auto rickshaw was going for the purpose of loading household articles of his brother from Nagavalli to Ripponpet.
Then, it is also amounting to deemed authorized representative of goods so as to cover risk under Section 147 of the M.V. Act.

In this regard, he placed reliance on the following judgments:
(1) MFA No.21/2017 and connected matters, 25.11.2022 between the Branch Manager, Cholamandalam General Insurance Company Limited vs. Gowramma and others.

sentences.text: 5. On the other hand, the learned counsel for the respondent-Insurance Company submitted that from the evidence of the claimant - PW1 herself and Ex.R6 - claim form, the goods Auto rickshaw was empty and in the said empty vehicle, the deceased was traveling.
Therefore, it is amounting to traveling as a gratuitous passenger.
Hence, the risk is not covered under Section 147 of the M.V. Act.
Therefore submitted that the Tribunal is correct in holding the owner is liable to pay the compensation.

Further submitted that even though in the claim petition, it is averred that there was goods in the auto rickshaw traveling from Ripponpet to Nagavalli, but the evidence of PW1 - claimant to the fact that the goods auto rickshaw was going from Ripponpet to Nagavalli for the purpose of loading luggage that amounts to auto rickshaw was coming to Nagavalli without load as it was empty.
Further submitted in the FIR and also in the charge sheet, it is mentioned that the goods auto rickshaw was empty.
Further in Ex.R6-claim form, the owner stated that the auto rickshaw was empty.
Hence, submitted in that empty vehicle, the deceased has traveled.

Therefore,
it does not amount to traveling as an authorized representative of goods.

Therefore, the risk is not covered as per Section 147 of the M.V. Act and it is correctly considered by the Tribunal and therefore submitted the judgment and award passed is justifiable, legal and correct one.
Hence prays for dismissal of the appeal.

6. In support of his arguments, he places reliance on the following judgments:
(1) (2008) 8 SC 246 - National Insurance Company Limited vs. Kaushalaya Devi and others.
(2) MFA No.3171/2007 - M/s. Oriental Insurance Company Limited vs. Rudrappa and another.

7. Upon hearing the rival submissions and on perusal of the records, the following point arises for consideration:
"Whether, under the facts and circumstances involved in the case, the Insurance Company is liable to be exonerated when the goods carriage vehicle was hired by the deceased for the purpose of loading the goods at a particular place and travelled in the said empty goods carriage vehicle and met with an accident and died and amounts to travelling as not authorized representative of the goods, thus, the Insurance Company is liable to be exonerated?"
8.

In the present case, the claimants averred in the claim petition that the deceased who is the husband of claimant No.1 examined as PW.1 had hired the goods autorickshaw and loaded the goods, which are household articles belonging to his brother-Ramu and while loading he travelled as an authorized representative of the goods from Ribbonpet to Nagavalli and died in the accident.

4 RW.1 who is the driver of the said goods autorickshaw has deposed that the goods autorickshaw was hired by the deceased and was loaded with household articles and while going from Ribbonpet to Nagavalli, the goods autorickshaw met with accident and the deceased died.

sentences.text: But claimant No.1 being the wife of the deceased while giving evidence as PW.1 has deposed in the evidence that her husband hired the autorickshaw to go from Ribbonpet to Nagavalli for the purpose of carrying goods of household articles belonging to his brother-Ramu and the deceased was travelling in the autorickshaw and while going from Ribbonpet to Nagavalli, the autorickshaw met with the accident and the deceased died.
9. Ex.R6 is the claim form submitted by the appellant-owner for claiming compensation to the Insurance Company, in which, it is stated that the vehicle was empty.

In the FIR and in the charge sheet, it is mentioned that the autorickshaw was going from Ribbonpet to Nagavalli for the purpose of loading household articles belonging to the brother of the deceased and while going from Ribbonpet to Nagavalli, the vehicle met with an accident and the deceased died.

The dissection of factual matrix involved as above discussed is essential for the purpose of interpretation of Section 147 of MV Act.
- 10 - 10.

Section 147 of MV Act stipulates as follows:
"147 Requirements of policies and limits of liability.

--(1) In order to comply with the requirements of this Chapter, a policy of insurance must be a policy which-- (a) is issued by a person who is an authorised insurer; and (b) insures the person or classes of persons specified in the policy to the extent specified in sub-section (2)--
(i) against any liability which may be incurred by him in respect of the death of or bodily 27 [injury to any person, including owner of the goods or his authorised representative carried in the vehicle] or damage to any property of a third party caused by or arising out of the use of the vehicle in a public place;
(ii) against the death of or bodily injury to any passenger of a public service vehicle caused by or arising out of the use of the vehicle in a public place:
Provided that a policy shall not be required-- (i) to cover liability in respect of the death, arising out of and in the course of his employment, of the employee of a person insured by the policy or in respect of bodily injury sustained by such an employee arising out of and in the course of his employment other than a liability arising under the Workmen's Compensation Act,
1923 (8 of 1923) in respect of the death of, or bodily injury to, any such employee-- Sri Gopalakrishna G Nayak vs Smt. Chandramathi on 21 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/195050742/
5 (a) engaged in driving the vehicle, or (b) if it is a public service vehicle engaged as conductor of the vehicle or in examining tickets on the vehicle, or (c) if it is a goods carriage, being carried in the vehicle, or - 11 - (ii) to cover any contractual liability.
Explanation.

sentences.text: --For the removal of doubts, it is hereby declared that the death of or bodily injury to any person or damage to any property of a third party shall be deemed to have been caused by or to have arisen out of, the use of a vehicle in a public place notwithstanding that the person who is dead or injured or the property which is damaged was not in a public place at the time of the accident, if the act or omission which led to the accident occurred in a public place.

(2) Subject to the proviso to sub-section (1), a policy of insurance referred to in sub-section (1), shall cover any liability incurred in respect of any accident, up to the following limits, namely:--
(a) save as provided in clause (b), the amount of liability incurred;
(b) in respect of damage to any property of a third party, a limit of rupees six thousand:
Provided that any policy of insurance issued with any limited liability and in force,
immediately before the commencement of this Act, shall continue to be effective for a period of four months after such commencement or till the date of expiry of such policy whichever is earlier.
(3) A policy shall be of no effect for the purposes of this Chapter unless and until there is issued by the insurer in favour of the person by whom the policy is effected a certificate of insurance in the prescribed form and containing the prescribed particulars of any condition subject to which the policy is issued and of any other prescribed matters; and different forms, particulars and matters may be prescribed in different cases.

(4) Where a cover note issued by the insurer under the provisions of this Chapter or the rules made thereunder is not followed by a policy of insurance within the prescribed time, the insurer shall, within seven days of the expiry of the period of the validity of the cover note, notify the fact to the registering authority in whose records the vehicle to which the cover note relates has - 12 - Sri Gopalakrishna G Nayak vs Smt. sentences.text: (5) Notwithstanding anything contained in any law for the time being in force, an insurer issuing a policy of insurance under this section shall be liable to indemnify the person or classes of persons specified in the policy in respect of any liability which the policy purports to cover in the case of that person or those classes of persons."

11. As per Section 147(1)(b)(i) of MV Act, the requirements of policies and limits of liability that there is compulsory coverage of insurance in respect of the person or classes of persons specified in the policy subject to Sub-section (2) of Section 147 of MV Act covering bodily injury to any person or death occurred including the owner of the goods or his authorized representative carried in the vehicle.

Therefore, the requirement of proof is that any injured or deceased has to travel in the goods vehicle either as owner of the goods or authorized representative of the goods, so as to cover under Section 147 of MV Act.
In the present case, the facts as revealed in the evidence on record are that the deceased had hired the goods autorickshaw and hiring of goods autorickshaw is admitted - 13 - and proved.
From the evidence on record, it is proved that the autorickshaw was going from Ribbonpet to Nagavalli.
But it is revealed from the factual matrix that either one of the fact may be correct, but not both.

Under the facts and circumstances involved in the case, either the goods autorickshaw was loaded with household articles belonging to Ramu who is the brother of the deceased or the deceased was travelling in the loaded goods autorickshaw and another fact is that the autorickshaw was going from Ribbonpet to Nagavalli for the purpose of loading household articles belonging to Ramu who is the brother of the deceased at Nagavalli and therefore, the goods autorickshaw at that particular point of way from Ribbonpet to Nagavalli was not yet loaded with household articles, but the deceased had travelled from Ribbonpet to Nagavalli.

But as discussed above, in the claim petition and from the evidence of R.W.1-driver of the autorickshaw, it is revealed that the autorickshaw was loaded with household articles and was going from Ribbonpet to Nagavalli.

But P.W.1 in her evidence - 14 - (claimant No.1 who is the wife of the deceased) has stated that the goods autorickshaw was hired by the deceased for the purpose of loading household articles at Nagavalli and while going from Ribbonpet to Nagavalli yet the autorickshaw was to be loaded and met with an accident and the deceased died.
Ex.P.6 is the claim form, in which also, it is stated that the goods autorickshaw was empty at the time of accident.
12. No doubt, the position of law is that, if there is no proof that the deceased had travelled along with the goods, then the Insurance Company is not liable.

But when the goods carriage vehicle is hired for the purpose of loading some objects from a particular point of place and while was going so met with an accident, under these circumstances, if death or bodily injury is caused to person,
whether amounts to travelled as authorized representative of the goods for the purpose of Sri Gopalakrishna G Nayak vs Smt. Chandramathi on 21 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/195050742/
7 interpretation of Section 147 of MV Act is to be considered.

sentences.text: The Hon'ble Supreme Court in Kaushalya Devi's case (stated supra) held that it was not proved that the deceased who was the owner of the goods was being carried in the truck, but the deceased was travelling in the truck for the purpose of collecting empty boxes.

Under that factual matrix, it was held that since there was no proof that the deceased had travelled along with the goods either as owner or authorized representative of the goods, therefore, in that context, it was held that the Insurance Company is not liable as it amounts that the deceased had travelled as a gratuitous passenger.
The factual matrix in the above stated case and in the present case are found to be different.
Therefore, the above stated judgment is not helpful to the Insurance Company.

14. Further this Court in the case of Rudrappa (stated supra) has observed and held that there was no evidence before the Tribunal that the claimant had hired the autorickshaw or he had Ragi to be transported in the - 16 - said autorickshaw.

Therefore, in the absence of these two factors that there is no proof of hiring the autorickshaw and there is no proof that Ragi was to be transported, therefore, under those facts and circumstances, it was held that the claimant had travelled as a gratuitous passenger.
Therefore, the finding that the Insurance Company is liable is not correct by making interpretation of Section 147 of MV Act.

But in the present case, it is proved that the deceased had hired the autorickshaw and also by considering the submission of learned counsel for the Insurance Company that the goods autorickshaw was still empty and was going from Ribbonpet to Nagavalli for the purpose of loading household articles at Nagavali and still before reaching Nagavalli, the goods autorickshaw was empty and therefore, when the goods even were to be loaded and transported, then if the deceased had travelled in the said autorickshaw even by hiring the autorickshaw for the purpose of loading the household articles, then it is amounting to travelling as not gratuitous passengers, but deemed representative of goods.
Therefore, under these - 17 - circumstances, the factual matrix in Rudrappa's case and in the present case is having two different set of facts.
Therefore, due to differences in this regard, the above said judgment is not applicable in the present case.

15. In Aishabi's case (stated supra) the facts are that the deceased had travelled in the lorry along with fish boxes and after unloading the fish boxes at Bhadravathi the deceased was returning in the said vehicle and the accident was occurred.
Under these facts and circumstances, this Court has held that when the accident was caused, the lorry was empty.
Therefore, it cannot be said that the deceased had travelled along with the goods as an authorized representative of the goods and therefore, held that the Insurance Company is not liable.

sentences.text: The expression used under Section 147 (1)(b)(i) of MV Act is "owner of goods or authorized representative of goods" in the present case does not - 18 - mean that the deceased had not travelled in the autorickshaw as representative of the goods.

After unloading or before loading the goods, when the goods vehicle is hired for the purpose of carrying of goods and travelling along with the goods, it means that the deceased had travelled either as owner or authorized representative of the goods.

If after unloading the goods or the vehicle was taken on hire for the purpose of loading the goods at a particular place and while going towards that place and for the purpose of loading the goods and before that met with an accident, then it amounts to deemed authorized representative of the goods.

Interpretation of travelling along with the goods as representative of the goods shall not be made in a literal sense, but should be considered in a realistic way that, if the vehicle is used for carrying of goods, yet to be loaded before the accident occurred, or after unloading the goods while returning, quite naturally, the vehicle was empty and then met with an accident, under such facts and circumstances also, it can be construed that the deceased - 19 - had travelled as an authorized representative of the goods.

In this regard, this Court in more or similar circumstances of the case in Gowramma's (stated supra) case at Paragraph Nos.15, 16 and 17 held as follows:
"15.

The words used in Section-147 of MV Act that traveling along with the goods not only means traveling along with goods when it is loaded, but also after unloading /
emptying the goods from the vehicle and returning in the same vehicle also amounts to traveling along with goods.

16. The judgment of the HIGH COURT OF JUDICATURE AT MADRAS, MADURAI BENCH, in the case of ORIENTAL INSURANCE CO. LTD. VS. NALLUCHAMY AND ANOTHERS2, while interpreting Section-147(1)(b)(i) at para Nos.12, 13, 14, 15, 16 and 17, has held as follows:
"12.As per Section 147(1)(b)(i), the Insurance Company is liable to pay in respect of death or bodily injury of any person including the owner of the goods or his authorised representative carried in the vehicle or damage to any property of a third party caused by or arising out of the use of the vehicle in a public place.
13.In this case, it has to be decided whether the Insurance Company is liable if on facts the owner or the authorized representative who travelled in the vehicle after unloading the vehicle died or suffered injuries, is entitled to be paid compensation from the Insurance Company.

It is not the case of the Insurance Company that the load auto did not carry the goods, ie., 3 bags of tomatoes of the claimant.
Their case is that after unloading only he travelled and therefore he is not covered.
15.The judgment relied on by the learned counsel for the appellant is of no use.

In that case, though the claimant made a claim that he travelled in the lorry along with the rice bags, this Court came to the conclusion that there was no evidence to claim that he travelled along with the goods.

In those circumstances, this Court in United India Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Annamalai, reported in 2011 (2) TN MAC 737 came to the conclusion that the Tribunal has erred infastening the liability on the Insurance Company when there is absolutely no evidence to the effect that the claimant travelled along with the goods in the lorry.

It is relevant to extract a portion of paragraph-5 of the said judgment, as under:
It is true that nothing happened when the goods were taken.
But the unfortunate incident took place while the lorry was returning after unloading the rice there.
17.In my view, the judgment of the Kerala High Court (cited supra), covers the issue.
Further, I am of the view that provisions of Section 147 of the Motor Vehicles Act has to be interpreted liberally and the main purpose is to grant compensation to the unfortunate accident victims.

Unless it is established by the Insurance Company that they are not at all liable, the Insurance Company cannot escape from its liability to pay compensation, particularly when it is admitted that the tomato bags carried by the load auto belongs to the claimant and he being an agriculturist, took these bags to the market and returned in the auto, which carried the tomato bags and that the said auto got involved in the accident at the time of return.
Hence, in my view the Insurance Company is liable to pay compensation."

17. Therefore, the issue involved in the present case is whether the insurance company is liable if the owner or the authorized representative of the goods after unloading or emptying the goods in the Sri Gopalakrishna G Nayak vs Smt. 10 market and while returning in the same goods vehicle died, which means actually traveling in the goods vehicle but also after unloading the said goods while returning in the vehicle means in the accident died is also amounting to traveling along with goods for the purpose of Section-147(1)(b)(i)
of MV Act."

sentences.text: This Court also in the case of Shakuntala (stated supra) has held that the coolie had travelled along with cement goods in the lorry and after unloading the said cement load and while returning in the same lorry met with an accident and under such circumstances, it was held that the deceased had travelled along with the goods as it is amounting to deemed authorized representative of the goods even after unloading the same.

Thus, the Insurance Company is held liable covering the risk as per Section 147 of MV Act.
18.
In the present case also, the deceased hired the autorickshaw going from Ribbonpet to Nagavalli and from Nagavalli to Ribbonpet is admitted.

Even the factual matrix involved in the present case as discussed above, even though, the autorickshaw was empty going from Ribbonpet to Nagavalli for the purpose of loading the household articles from Nagavalli and met with an accident, under such circumstances also, it is amounting - 23 - that the deceased had travelled as an authorized representative of the goods to be loaded/transported from Nagavalli.
Therefore, under these principles and as interpreted under Section 147 of MV Act, the Insurance Company cannot avoid its liability to pay the compensation.

In order to cover the risk under Section 147 of MV Act it is not only that the person actually shall travel physically along with the goods, but when the deceased had hired the autorickshaw for the purpose of loading the goods and while taking the said goods vehicle for the purpose of loading the goods,
even though, at that particular point of time of the accident, the accident was caused, it is amounting to travelling as an authorized representative of the goods, even though, the goods were yet to be loaded or transported.
The autorickshaw was taken on hire for specific purpose by the deceased for transporting the household articles from Nagavalli to Ribbonpet.
Therefore, it cannot be said that the deceased had travelled as gratuitous passenger.
Under these circumstances, it is held that the Insurance Company is not liable to be exonerated.

Therefore, in the present set of facts and circumstances, even though, Section 147 of MV Act is interpreted, one thing is proved that the deceased had travelled along with the goods and another thing is that the goods were yet to be loaded or transported.

But the fact remains proved that the deceased had hired the autorickshaw for the specific purpose of loading and transporting of household articles from Nagavalli, therefore, under both these circumstances, the Insurance Company is liable to indemnify the owner as there is undisputedly coverage of insurance as on the date of the accident.

Therefore, the Tribunal is not correct in exonerating the Insurance Company Sri Gopalakrishna G Nayak vs Smt. Chandramathi on 21 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/195050742/
11 and fastening the liability on the appellant-owner to pay compensation.

7. Upon hearing the rival submissions and on perusal of the records, the following point arises for consideration:
"Whether, under the facts and circumstances involved in the case, the Insurance Company is liable to be exonerated when the goods carriage vehicle was hired by the deceased for the purpose of loading the goods at a particular place and travelled in the said empty goods carriage vehicle and met with an accident and died and amounts to travelling as not authorized representative of the goods, thus, the Insurance Company is liable to be exonerated?"

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
11. As per Section 147(1)(b)(i) of MV Act, the requirements of policies and limits of liability that there is compulsory coverage of insurance in respect of the person or classes of persons specified in the policy subject to Sub-section (2) of Section 147 of MV Act covering bodily injury to any person or death occurred including the owner of the goods or his authorized representative carried in the vehicle.
Therefore, the requirement of proof is that any injured or deceased has to travel in the goods vehicle either as owner of the goods or authorized representative of the goods, so as to cover under Section 147 of MV Act.
But when the goods carriage vehicle is hired for the purpose of loading some objects from a particular point of place and while was going so met with an accident, under these circumstances, if death or bodily injury is caused to person,
whether amounts to travelled as authorized representative of the goods for the purpose of Sri Gopalakrishna G Nayak vs Smt. Chandramathi on 21 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/195050742/
7 interpretation of Section 147 of MV Act is to be considered.
But in the present case, it is proved that the deceased had hired the autorickshaw and also by considering the submission of learned counsel for the Insurance Company that the goods autorickshaw was still empty and was going from Ribbonpet to Nagavalli for the purpose of loading household articles at Nagavali and still before reaching Nagavalli, the goods autorickshaw was empty and therefore, when the goods even were to be loaded and transported, then if the deceased had travelled in the said autorickshaw even by hiring the autorickshaw for the purpose of loading the household articles, then it is amounting to travelling as not gratuitous passengers, but deemed representative of goods.
Sri Gopalakrishna G Nayak vs Smt. Chandramathi on 21 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/195050742/
8 16.
The expression used under Section 147 (1)(b)(i) of MV Act is "owner of goods or authorized representative of goods" in the present case does not - 18 - mean that the deceased had not travelled in the autorickshaw as representative of the goods.
After unloading or before loading the goods, when the goods vehicle is hired for the purpose of carrying of goods and travelling along with the goods, it means that the deceased had travelled either as owner or authorized representative of the goods.
Interpretation of travelling along with the goods as representative of the goods shall not be made in a literal sense, but should be considered in a realistic way that, if the vehicle is used for carrying of goods, yet to be loaded before the accident occurred, or after unloading the goods while returning, quite naturally, the vehicle was empty and then met with an accident, under such facts and circumstances also, it can be construed that the deceased - 19 - had travelled as an authorized representative of the goods.

Even the factual matrix involved in the present case as discussed above, even though, the autorickshaw was empty going from Ribbonpet to Nagavalli for the purpose of loading the household articles from Nagavalli and met with an accident, under such circumstances also, it is amounting - 23 - that the deceased had travelled as an authorized representative of the goods to be loaded/transported from Nagavalli.
Therefore, under these principles and as interpreted under Section 147 of MV Act, the Insurance Company cannot avoid its liability to pay the compensation.
In order to cover the risk under Section 147 of MV Act it is not only that the person actually shall travel physically along with the goods, but when the deceased had hired the autorickshaw for the purpose of loading the goods and while taking the said goods vehicle for the purpose of loading the goods,
even though, at that particular point of time of the accident, the accident was caused, it is amounting to travelling as an authorized representative of the goods, even though, the goods were yet to be loaded or transported.
The autorickshaw was taken on hire for specific purpose by the deceased for transporting the household articles from Nagavalli to Ribbonpet.
But the fact remains proved that the deceased had hired the autorickshaw for the specific purpose of loading and transporting of household articles from Nagavalli, therefore, under both these circumstances, the Insurance Company is liable to indemnify the owner as there is undisputedly coverage of insurance as on the date of the accident.
